definition: The acceleration phase of a Pulse transit departure — the 47 seconds during which the slug goes from rest to Mach 6 across 11 kilometers of acceleration corridor. Experienced as a gentle but persistent pressure pushing passengers back into their reclined seats, approximately the sensation of a steep elevator rise, sustained just long enough to become unsettling. For unaugmented or lightly augmented passengers, 'the punch' is more literal — the GIDS field has fewer coupling points and the effective g-force is higher.
origin: Pulse passenger slang; in use since the second-generation network opened (circa 2167)
usage: Used by frequent Pulse travelers. First-timers rarely have a word for it until they've experienced it and need to describe it to someone who hasn't.
tier: Tier 3-5 (those who actually ride the Pulse)
example: "Relax into the punch — don't grip the armrests, it doesn't help and you'll feel worse."
